- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A gramby roll is a technique in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ) that involves using a rolling motion to escape from the bottom side control position.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The gramby roll is named after Marcelo Garcia, who is a Brazilian BJJ practitioner and instructor known for his effective use of the technique.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To execute the gramby roll, you start by lying on your back with your opponent in the side control position on top of you.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] You use your hips and legs to create space and leverage, and roll your body over onto your side.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] As you roll, you can use your arms to control your opponent's head and posture, and to prevent them from following you and re-establishing the side control position.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The gramby roll is an effective technique for escaping from the bottom side control position and taking the top position.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It requires good coordination, control, and timing, and can be challenging to execute against a resisting opponent.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] With practice, you can develop the skills and confidence needed to successfully execute the gramby roll in BJJ.
